action: press 'Return' -- sign off the finished sheet from the summary page
commentary: Nought left over and nothing overdrawn. Forty-seven years, a wrecked back, ears like a bat and a head full of steam plant. Every line on that page is one I put there myself. Sign it.

action: press 'Tab' -- step forward off the summary page, which is what raises the last question
commentary: One more page forward and the form will ask me if I am sure.

action: press 'Y' -- answer Yes to the last question on the form and go out the door
commentary: Yes. I am sure. The sheet reads back true and there is nothing left on it I would change. Open the door.

action: press 'i' -- look through what I am actually carrying before I do anything else
commentary: Count what you have before you plan anything. First rule of every job I ever ran.

action: press 'Escape' -- close the list and get on with it
commentary: A phone with a full battery, a wallet with six dollars in it, and my father's watch on my wrist. The watch is the only one of the three worth anything now.

action: press 'k' -- step one tile north, toward the cupboard on the far wall
commentary: Very dark in here and I am not going to learn anything standing still. There is a cupboard on the north wall and cupboards are where people keep things.

action: press 'k' -- step north again to reach the cupboard wall
commentary: Two steps. Quietly. My ears are better than my eyes in this and there is nothing moving in the house that I can hear.

action: press 'e' -- ask what the furniture beside me actually is before I start pulling at it
commentary: Do not yank a drawer you have not looked at. Look first.

action: press 'h' -- step west toward the mirror and the basin I can make out on that wall
commentary: Water first. There is a mirror on the west wall and where there is a mirror there is a basin, and where there is a basin there is a trap under it with water still standing in it.

action: press 'h' -- step west again
commentary: Two steps west. Slowly.

action: press 'b' -- step south-west to bring the basin within reach
commentary: Round the corner of the wall.

action: press 'e' -- ask what the fittings in this little room are
commentary: A bathroom. There is a cistern on a toilet and a trap under a basin and both of them hold water that has not been through anything since the pumps stopped.

action: press 'k' -- step north onto the tile beside the cistern, away from the moaning
commentary: Something is moaning north-east of me and I am not going to walk at it with my hands empty. But the cistern is north and I need the water more than I need to be clever.

action: press 'e' -- ask the cistern what is in it
commentary: Lift the lid. There is a gallon in the tank of any toilet in this country and none of it has been through a pump since Sunday.

action: press 'n' -- step south-east off the mirror, back toward the room with the bed in it
commentary: Off this glass. Something is moaning to the north-east and the only room in this house with a door I can shut is the one with the bed in it.

action: press 'n' -- keep moving south-east toward the bedroom
commentary: Two steps. Count the exits as you go: the lit doorway south, the way I came in west, and whatever is north-east that I have not seen.

action: press 'l' -- step east into the bedroom
commentary: In.

action: press 'Escape' -- back out of the panel the mirror put in front of me
commentary: I have not moved an inch. That was no cistern I lifted the lid on -- it is a standing mirror, and the thing I have been looking into for five breaths is my own face. Forty-seven years old and grey at the temple and that is the woman who has to do this. Back out of it.

action: press 'a' -- ask what of mine can be put to use
commentary: It is eight in the morning and I cannot see the far wall of a bathroom, so the first tool is the one already in my pocket. My phone has a lamp in it. It has a charge in it too, and no tower left to spend that charge on.

action: press 'Return' -- take the phone out and ask it what it can still do
commentary: Fifty-six out of fifty-six on the battery. Charged it Wednesday night out of habit, the way I have every night for eleven years, and Wednesday night is the last ordinary thing I did.

action: press '0' -- turn on the phone's flashlight
commentary: Eight things it offers me and seven of them are for a world with people still in it. Calorie tracker. Play a game. Play music. The eighth is a lamp, and that is the one that is worth anything now.

action: press 'k' -- step north to the toilet now that I can see it
commentary: And there is the room, all of it at once. A toilet one step north of me. A refrigerator past that. A bed through the doorway east with two pillows still on it. Somebody lived here on Wednesday.

action: press 'l' -- go round to the east instead, since straight north is blocked
commentary: North is stopped up -- the toilet is squarely in the way and I am not climbing over porcelain in the dark. Round it to the east. Twenty-two years of walking a mill floor teaches you that the shortest line is the one you can actually put your feet on.

action: press 'e' -- ask what is worth examining from here
commentary: Off the glass and I can read the room properly. That is my own mirror behind me, a tub in the corner, and a bed through the gap in the wall. And a pool of somebody on the floor two feet from my boot. I am not going to pretend I did not see it.

action: press 'Escape' -- shut the mirror panel again
commentary: The mirror keeps putting itself forward. It is the nearest thing to my left hand and the house cannot tell the difference between what I am reaching for and what is closest. Fine. I will stand somewhere the glass is not the first thing I touch.

action: press 'k' -- step north so the toilet is the thing directly beside me
commentary: North one. Now the cistern is straight off my left shoulder and the mirror is behind me at an angle.

action: press 'e' -- examine what is beside me now that the toilet is the nearest thing
commentary: There is a door north of me too, shut, and a tub behind it somewhere. But the cistern first. A house loses its taps in a day and keeps a gallon in every toilet tank for a week.

action: press 'Escape' -- close the mirror panel and stop asking this room questions
commentary: Twice more and I have my answer, and it is not the one I wanted. That white thing beside me is a basin, not a cistern -- a vanity sink with two taps and nothing behind them. No pumps, no pressure, no water. This is a bathroom with a mirror, a tub and a dry sink, and the only thing in it worth having is the door.

action: press 'o' -- open the door north out of the bathroom
commentary: So: the door. Out first, water later.

action: press 'l' -- step east onto the tile where the socks are lying
commentary: The door out of this room is on my left and it is already standing open, which is why nothing here can be opened. Somebody left in a hurry. East then, over the blood, to the two white things on the floor.

action: press 'g' -- pick up what is on this tile
commentary: A pair of ankle socks. Poor fit, and I do not care. I have steel toecaps on and nothing between them and my skin, and by tonight that would have been two raw heels and a limp. You take the socks.

action: press 'W' -- put the socks straight on rather than carry them
commentary: The pile lists one thing and the panel offers to put it on me directly instead of into my hands. Do that. An item in a pocket is a thing I own; an item on my foot is a thing that is working.

action: press 'u' -- step north-east past the chair into the next room
commentary: Socks on. Now the room east of me, because there is a chair in it and a bed and something small lying on the floor two steps past the chair with a handle on it. Handles are what I am looking for.

action: press 'l' -- step east to the small thing with the handle
commentary: Whatever it is, it has a shaft and a head, and that is the shape of every useful object ever made.

action: press 'g' -- pick up the thing on this tile
commentary: A vegetable peeler. Not a knife, not a screwdriver -- a peeler. And I will take it, because it is a fixed blade on a handle and a scraper on the other side, and out of the two hundred objects in this house it is the first one that is a tool rather than a decoration.

action: press 'w' -- take the peeler up into my hand rather than into a pocket
commentary: Into the hand, not the pocket. I have been walking round a dead house with my fists and there is something moaning north-east of here. A peeler is a poor answer to that but it is an answer, and it is the difference between reaching for something and having it.

action: press 'h' -- step west back past the chair
commentary: It has moved. It was north-east of me when I woke up in this house and now it is north-west, which means it is walking and I am not the only thing in Fern Creek that got up this morning. There is a wardrobe three steps west of me and wardrobes are where people keep bags.

action: press 'h' -- keep going west toward the wardrobe
commentary: Two.

action: press 'h' -- step onto the open doorway with the wardrobe due north of me
commentary: Three, and I am standing in the doorway with the wardrobe on my right hand. Doorways are bad places to stand. I will not be here long.

action: press 'j' -- give up on the wardrobe and go south instead
commentary: Two shoves at the wall and I got nowhere -- I did not walk three steps west, I walked one, onto a chair, and then stood there pushing at a bathtub. The wardrobe is behind a tub and a doorway I cannot reach from this side. So: no bag. Say it plainly and stop spending daylight on it. South instead. There is a bed down there and a bed is worth more to me today than a bag.

action: press 'j' -- step south over the edge of the blood toward the bed
commentary: Off the chair and south. The blood runs out under my boot here and I am walking round the wide part of it, not through it, because I have no idea yet whether whatever made it is still in the building.

action: press 'j' -- step south onto the foot of the bed
commentary: And there is the bed. Grey blanket folded back on the near side, pillow on the far side, and a toilet in the corner past the foot of it -- which means this is not a bedroom, this is somebody's bed put in the room with the plumbing. Or the wall came down. Either way there is water in that cistern.

action: press 'e' -- examine the toilet standing at the corner of the bed
commentary: There it is properly, white and square in the corner off the foot of the bed, and this time it is a toilet and not a vanity basin. Lift the lid on the tank. Nothing has been through that water since the pumps had pressure and there is the better part of a gallon of it.

action: press 'g' -- open the pile of things lying on this tile
commentary: Nothing beside me can be examined, which settles it: the white thing in the corner is not plumbing, it is an object sitting on the floor. Later. There is a floral blanket under my boots and this house is going to be cold at three in the morning with no furnace running.

action: press '5' -- answer the direction prompt with my own tile
commentary: It wants to know which square. This one, under my own feet.

action: press 'Escape' -- leave the blanket where it lies
commentary: Does not fit in any pocket. Of course it does not. The only way to take it is to put it on, and a blanket on my shoulders is forty points of clumsy with something walking around the house. It stays on the bed. That is where I will be at three in the morning and that is where it needs to be.

action: press 'b' -- step south-west to the white thing on the floor
commentary: Now the other thing. South-west, the white object in the corner that could not be examined because it is not fixed to the house.

action: press 'g' -- ask for what is lying here
commentary: An undershirt. Not a bucket, not a pot, not a jug. A man's undershirt on the floor beside the bed, poor fit, and it is the third time that thing has moaned at me from the north-west while I stand in a stranger's bedroom picking his laundry up off the floor.

action: press '5' -- this tile
commentary: Here.

action: press 'W' -- put the undershirt on under what I am already wearing
commentary: On, under the shirt. It is a layer, and layers are the whole argument at four in the morning when the house is the same temperature as the yard. I came out of Thursday morning with a phone, a wallet and my father's watch. I now have socks, a shirt and a blade. That is not nothing.

action: press 'u' -- step north-east back onto the bed
commentary: Back onto the bed. Not to lie down. To sit on the edge of it with my back to the outside wall and my face to the doorway, which is the only way anything can come at me in this room, and think for a minute instead of walking about in a dead man's house making noise.

action: press 'bar' -- ask the game to let time pass while I sit still and listen
commentary: Here is the arithmetic. No water, no bag, no weapon worth the name, a bad back, and I am slow. It is moaning north-west and it has not found me. The worst thing I can do is walk about. The best thing I can do is sit still, keep quiet and let it wander off, and then use the daylight. So: sit. Listen. Count.

action: press 'w' -- choose to wait a while rather than set an alarm
commentary: It asks whether I want to wait or set an alarm, and it only asks because I am carrying something that keeps time. My father's watch on my left wrist and a phone in my pocket, and between them I know exactly what hour it is in a town where nobody else does. Wait a while.

action: press '3' -- wait five minutes
commentary: It offers me twenty seconds up to six hours and it tells me it is 08:00:27. Five minutes to start. Not because five minutes is a plan but because five minutes is how long you listen to a strange noise before you decide what it is.

action: press 'bar' -- ask to wait again now the five minutes are up
commentary: Five minutes gone and the watch says so. It has not come through the doorway. It has not got any louder. Whatever it is, it is walking a circle somewhere on the other side of that wall and it does not know I am here. Again, then, and longer this time.

action: press 'I' -- tell the house I have heard the groaning and choose to keep sitting anyway
commentary: Correct myself: the five minutes did not pass. The watch still says 08:00:27. I had barely settled when it heard the groaning for me and stopped the clock to ask whether I wanted to stop too, and the second time I reached for the same key it would not take it, because a question was standing in front of it. Yes. I heard it. I have heard it four times now and it has not once come through that doorway. I am going to sit here and let it groan.

action: press 'k' -- get up off the bed and go north
commentary: The five minutes did pass in the end and it is 08:05 and it still has not come through the doorway. Sitting was the right call and I am not going to keep making it, because sitting does not get me water. There is a refrigerator in the room north-west of here. Whatever a stranger had in his fridge on Wednesday afternoon is still in it on Thursday morning, and some of it will be wet.

action: press 'k' -- keep going north
commentary: North again. Quietly. Heel down first, then the weight, the way you cross a mill floor at three in the morning when the night shift is asleep in the break room.

action: press 'h' -- step west across the blood to get within reach of the refrigerator
commentary: West, across the near edge of the blood. I can see the front of the refrigerator from here: two handles, freezer over cold box, the same unit half of New England bought in 2009. It is diagonally in front of my left shoulder and I do not need to open it to reach into it.

action: press 'g' -- ask for what is inside the refrigerator
commentary: Reach in.

action: press 'l' -- step back east because the way north from here is a bathtub
commentary: Empty. Both of them. I put my hand into a refrigerator and a wardrobe belonging to a man whose blood I am standing in and there is not one object in either of them. Somebody has been through this house already and they were thorough and they were not me. Fine. There are two sets of shelving at the top of this room and I can see things on the wooden one from here.

action: press 'k' -- go north past the chair toward the shelving
commentary: North. Past the chair.

action: press 'k' -- keep going north to come alongside the shelves
commentary: And again.

action: press 'g' -- ask for what is on the shelving in front of me
commentary: Two units of shelving, straight in front of me and one off to the right, and there is something on the boards of both. After a fridge and a wardrobe with nothing in them I am not going to get my hopes up, but shelves are the part of a house people forget to empty.

action: press 'm' -- open the map and find out where in the town I actually am
commentary: Nothing on the shelves either. Nothing in the fridge, nothing in the wardrobe, nothing on the boards, and I have been standing on a desk to find that out. This house is a shell. Before I spend one more minute in it I want to know what is around it, so: the map. Twenty-two years of shift work and the first thing you do on an unfamiliar site is find the exits.

action: press 'Escape' -- close the map now that I have read it
commentary: Mount Chase. I had the name wrong in my own head all morning and there it is in yellow letters across the middle of it. I am in a house in the northwest corner, there is a grid of streets under me, and there are two dozen roofs within three blocks including a row of big yellow ones south-east that are not houses. That is tomorrow. Close it.

action: press 'j' -- head back south toward the bed
commentary: Now the honest arithmetic, out loud, because I am the only one left to say it to. It is ten past eight in the morning on the twenty-eighth of May. I have a blade the length of my finger, a phone with a lamp in it, my father's watch, socks, and a shirt off a stranger's floor. I have no water. I have no bag. I am fifty pounds heavier than I should be and my back has been going since 2019.

action: press 'j' -- keep going south
commentary: I am not walking into a street I have never seen with a vegetable peeler in my fist because I am thirsty in an hour's time. Thirst takes days. A street takes seconds. So today I stay in this shell, out of sight, and I go out tomorrow at first light with a full night behind me instead of an hour.

action: press 'j' -- step south to the edge of the bed
commentary: Two more south and I am back at the bed. Same bed, same folded blanket, same pillow that belongs to somebody whose blood is four feet away, and I am going to use all three of them because being sentimental about a mattress is how you end up sleeping on a floor at forty-seven with a bad back.

action: press 'j' -- step onto the bed
commentary: On it. Back to the outside wall, face to the doorway.

action: press 'a' -- open the list of things I can put to use
commentary: One more piece of housekeeping before I settle. That lamp has been burning since eight o'clock for a room I have now looked at from every corner, and there is no wall socket in New England with anything behind it. Fifty-six charges is every hour of light I will ever have again until I find a way to make more.

action: press 'Return' -- choose the phone again
commentary: The phone.

action: press '6' -- turn the flashlight off
commentary: Off. It is going to be black in here and I am going to sit in it, and that is the correct trade. I know this room now. I know the doorway is on my left and the tub is behind the wall in front of me and there is nothing else in it. Light does not help you listen.

action: press 'bar' -- ask to let time pass again
commentary: Dark. Completely dark, and quieter than I expected, and I can hear my own watch. Right. Settle in properly this time. Not five minutes. Hours.

action: press 'w' -- choose to wait rather than set an alarm
commentary: Wait, not an alarm. I do not need waking. I need the day to go past me without me in the middle of it.

action: press '7' -- wait three hours
commentary: Three hours. Eight in the morning to eleven, sitting on a dead man's bed in the dark with a peeler in my lap, listening to a house. If somebody had told me on Wednesday that this was Thursday I would have laughed at them.

action: press 'I' -- tell it again that the moaning is not a reason to stand up
commentary: Sixty-six seconds into three hours and it stopped me to ask about the moaning. It will ask every time. So I will tell it every time. I have heard that noise five times in six minutes of sitting and not once has it got nearer. It is not a reason to stand up. It is the weather now.

action: press 'I' -- ignore the withdrawal as well and stay sitting
commentary: It got twenty-nine percent of the way through the three hours before the next thing stopped it, and this one is mine, not the town's. Withdrawals. Twenty-six years of a pack a day and the last one I smoked was on the back step on Wednesday night with the mill lights still on across the water. There is no tobacco in this house. There is no tobacco anywhere I can reach today. So this is what the rest of the week is going to feel like and I may as well start getting used to it sitting down.

action: press 'bar' -- set myself to wait again now the morning is gone
commentary: Eleven o'clock and five minutes. Three hours sat in the dark on a stranger's bed and the log of it is one line repeated forty times: from the north you hear moaning, from the north you hear groaning. North. Always north. It never once said west, which is the wall I have my shoulder against. It is out at the front of the house and it is staying there.

action: press 'w' -- choose to wait rather than set an alarm
commentary: Wait.

action: press '8' -- wait six hours
commentary: Six hours this time. Eleven to five in the afternoon. That takes me to the end of the useful daylight without me having spent any of it, which sounds like nothing and is actually the only thing I have done right today.

action: press 'I' -- ignore the withdrawal again
commentary: It asked before the six hours had even started this time. Withdrawals. Yes. I know. Sit down.

action: press 'I' -- ignore the moaning again and hold the six hours
commentary: And the moaning, thirteen seconds after that. Both of them at once now, the town outside and the want inside, taking turns to tell me to get up. No. Six hours. Hold it.

action: press 'a' -- open the list of things I can use again
commentary: Five past five in the afternoon and the sidebar has gone yellow at me: very thirsty. Peckish I can argue with. Very thirsty at five in the afternoon with no water in the building is not something you sleep on and sort out in the morning, because in the morning it says dehydrated and then it stops asking politely. I have three hours of light left outside and I have not looked at the south end of this house at all. Phone.

action: press 'Return' -- choose the phone
commentary: The phone again.

action: press '0' -- turn the flashlight back on
commentary: Light. And I am going to spend it, not hoard it, because a full battery is worth nothing to a woman who has been dead of thirst for two days.

action: press 'j' -- get off the bed and start south down the room
commentary: And now the log tells me what the afternoon was really like. Groaning from the south. Groaning from the east, twice. A crash from the south-east and above, which means there is a floor over my head and something on it. And in between all of that, four times: you need some nicotine. Speed ninety-four instead of a hundred and focus eighty-two. That is the cigarettes talking. Move.

action: press 'j' -- keep going south
commentary: There is a wall across the bottom of this room with a door in it and I have never once been through it. Five hours I sat twenty feet from a door I had not opened.

action: press 'j' -- keep going south toward that wall
commentary: Three.

action: press 'n' -- step south-east to stand square in front of the door
commentary: There is a houseplant on the floor to my right, alive, green, in a pot, which means somebody was watering it up until about Sunday. And there is the door, one south and one east of me. Square up to it.

action: press 'o' -- open the door
commentary: Hand on it. Slowly, and listen through it first, because everything I have heard for the last nine hours came from the far side of a wall and this is the first one I am going to open on purpose.

action: press 'j' -- step into the doorway itself and look out from inside the frame
commentary: Nothing to open. It is already standing open, like the other one, like every door in this house. Somebody went through this place and left every door in it wide. So I will stand in the frame of it and look out from inside the house rather than walk out into a yard I cannot see.

action: press 'j' -- step through the doorway and go south down the passage
commentary: I am an idiot and I am going to write that down. That is not the outside of the house. That is a passage, and at the end of it, four squares from where I have been sitting since half past eight this morning, there is a white bowl with a tank on the back of it and a basin with two taps. A toilet. There has been a toilet in this house all day.

action: press 'j' -- keep going south toward it
commentary: Go. Carefully, but go.

action: press 'j' -- step into the second doorway with the toilet on my left
commentary: Correction: the first push south did nothing, I was still in the frame of the upstairs door. This one moved me. And now I can see the whole of it -- toilet on the left, washer in the middle, laundry sink with two taps on the right, a tub past that, and a black bag sitting on a counter three squares east of me. Water first. Everything else after water.

action: press 'e' -- examine what is around me in this doorway
commentary: Left hand side. The tank.

action: press 'j' -- step out of the door frame and into the laundry itself
commentary: Reaching from the door frame got me nothing -- the tank is on the diagonal and you cannot reach round a door jamb, which anybody who has ever tried to get a wrench onto a fitting inside a bulkhead already knows. So stop reaching and walk in.

action: press 'e' -- examine the toilet now that it is square on my left
commentary: In, and the tank is straight off my left hand. There is water standing in the bowl and it is blue, which means somebody dropped one of those cistern blocks in it, which means the tank has not been touched. Examine it.

action: press 'h' -- answer the direction prompt with west, at the toilet
commentary: It asks where. West. And it turns out I am standing on a book of essays, four hundred pages of somebody's opinions, which I will come back for because paper burns and a fire boils water.

action: press 'E' -- ask what there is to drink within reach
commentary: Examining it told me nothing at all -- no menu, no message, and my move counter went to zero, so something happened and the house did not think it worth telling me about. Try it from the other end. Not what is the toilet, but what can I drink.

action: press 'Escape' -- close the list and take that answer
commentary: There it is in black and white. Very thirsty, and the complete list of everything I can drink within arm's reach of a toilet, a laundry sink and a bathtub is three doses of cold liquid soap. Nothing today, nothing yesterday, zero calories, zero iron, zero vitamin C. The taps are dead, the tank is dry and the blue in that bowl is a picture of water, not water.

action: press 'g' -- ask what is on the tiles around me
commentary: There is one thing left on this side of the house I have not put my hand on. Something pale blue sitting on the crate to my right.

action: press 'l' -- answer the prompt with east, at the crate
commentary: East.

action: press 'a' -- mark the plastic bottle to be taken
commentary: A wooden rack, one square east, and on it a plastic soap bottle and a sewing kit. I have been round this house all day looking for something to carry water in and it has been sitting on a laundry rack four feet from a bathtub the whole time. The soap I can pour out. The bottle is the thing.

action: press 'b' -- mark the sewing kit as well
commentary: Bottle is on the list. Now the sewing kit, eighty-nine yards of thread in it, and take that too. Everything I am wearing came off a stranger's floor and does not fit, and a needle is how clothes stay clothes.

action: press 'Return' -- confirm and take both of them
commentary: Both. Confirm.

action: press 'g' -- ask the rack again, because only one of the two came
commentary: Never mind, it said, and then it gave me the sewing kit and not the bottle. Marking the second thing threw the first one off the list. So do it again and do it one at a time, which is how you should do anything that matters.

action: press 'l' -- east, at the rack again
commentary: East again.

action: press 'I' -- ignore the withdrawal and finish the pickup
commentary: Not now. Stop picking up, it asks me, because my hands want a cigarette. No. Finish the job.

action: press 'g' -- ask for the book I am standing on
commentary: Got it. One plastic soap bottle, three doses of soap still in it, and a sewing kit, and seven and a half pounds on me instead of five. I have something to put water in. I do not have water, but I have the thing that holds it, and those are two different problems and only one of them was going to be solved indoors. Now the book under my boot.

action: press '5' -- this tile, the one I am standing on
commentary: This square.

action: press 'a' -- mark the book of essays
commentary: Book of essays, forty pages worth of somebody being certain about things. One item, one mark, and this time I am not going to press a second letter and lose the first.

action: press 'Return' -- confirm and take the book
commentary: Take it. Not to read. Dry paper is the difference between a pile of wet sticks and a fire, and a fire is the difference between a bottle of pond water and a bottle of water I can drink.

action: press 'k' -- start back north toward the bed
commentary: Right. Bottle, kit, book, blade. That is the day. Now north, back up the passage to the bed, because it is ten past five and I am not starting anything new at ten past five with a walker somewhere east of me and three hours of light left.

action: press 'k' -- keep going north up the passage
commentary: Two.

action: press 'k' -- keep going north
commentary: Three.

action: press 'k' -- keep going north
commentary: Four.

action: press 'k' -- step out of the door frame into the bedroom side
commentary: I am in the frame of the door again and there is a light fitting hanging over the passage ahead of me and something like a cylinder off to the right that I am not going to walk over and look at tonight. Step out of the frame first.

action: press 'c' -- close the door behind me
commentary: And now the thing I have wanted since eight o'clock this morning. Close it. Every door in this house has been standing open all day, including the one I slept next to, and I am going to put one of them back where it belongs with me on this side of it.

action: press 'k' -- carry on north toward the bed with the door shut behind me
commentary: There. A latch between me and the south half of the house. It is a hollow interior door and a determined child could go through it, but it is a noise I will hear before I feel it, and that is the whole difference.

action: press 'k' -- keep going north
commentary: Two more and I am at the bed.

action: press 'k' -- step onto the foot of the bed
commentary: Two steps and there it is again. Mattress, pillow, and the floral blanket still folded back on the near corner exactly where I left it at half past eight this morning.

action: press 'y' -- step north-west onto the corner where the blanket is
commentary: North-west, onto the blanket. This morning I would not put it on because forty points of clumsy is no way to walk round a house with something moaning in it. I am not walking anywhere now.

action: press 'g' -- ask for what is on this corner of the bed
commentary: There is a potato masher lying on the mattress I just walked over, which I am going to leave exactly where it is, because I have a blade and a needle and there is a limit to how much of a dead man's kitchen I am prepared to carry. The blanket, though. The blanket I want.

action: press '5' -- this square
commentary: Here.

action: press 'W' -- put the blanket on
commentary: On. Round the shoulders and over the top of a shirt that is not mine and an undershirt that is not mine either, and I am past caring about that too.

action: press 'a' -- open the list of things to use one last time
commentary: Blanket on. One last piece of housekeeping and then I am done with today.

action: press 'Return' -- choose the phone
commentary: The phone.

action: press '6' -- turn the flashlight off for the night
commentary: Off. It has been burning since five o'clock and I want every hour of it I can keep, and a light in a window is an advertisement. I know where the door is. I know where the wall is. I do not need to see to lie down.

action: press 'Escape' -- back out of the sewing kit by mistake
commentary: Wrong thing. The list is not the same list it was this morning -- I have a needle and a bottle and a book in my pockets now, so the top of it is the sewing kit and not the phone, and I have just asked a sewing kit to turn a flashlight off. Out.

action: press 'a' -- open the list again and look at it properly this time
commentary: Again, and this time read it before pressing anything. That is the second time today I have reached for something without looking and both times it cost me nothing. One day it will cost me a hand.

action: press 'Down' -- move down the list to the phone
commentary: Sewing kit on the top line, phone on the second. Fifty-three of fifty-six on the battery, so nine hours of that lamp cost me three charges, which is far better than I feared and does not change what I am about to do. Down one.

action: press 'Return' -- choose the phone
commentary: The phone.

action: press '6' -- turn the flashlight off for the night
commentary: Off. Properly this time.

action: press 'bar' -- set myself to wait out the last of the daylight
commentary: Ten past five is not a bedtime. I am not tired, I am thirsty, and lying down in daylight with my eyes open is how you spend a night staring at a ceiling. So sit again until the light is gone properly, and then lie down.

action: press 'w' -- wait rather than set an alarm
commentary: Wait.

action: press '7' -- wait three hours, until about eight
commentary: Three hours. That puts me at ten past eight with the sun off the roofs and the room the same dark it was this morning. Then I will lie down and see whether that works at all, because I have not slept a night through since about 2016 and there is no reason tonight should be the exception.

action: press 'I' -- ignore the withdrawal and hold the three hours
commentary: Withdrawals again, straight away. Nine hours of that now. Hold it.

action: press 'I' -- ignore the grunting as well and stay where I am
commentary: Grunting this time, not moaning. That is a different noise from a different throat and I am writing it down because it means there is more than one of them out there and they do not all sound the same. Still not a reason to stand up. Hold it.

action: press 'dollar' -- lie down and try to sleep
commentary: Six minutes past eight and the sidebar has stopped being polite. Dehydrated, in red. Strength nine instead of ten, dexterity six instead of seven, intelligence eleven, perception eight. Every number I have is one lower than it was this morning and that is what a day without water does to a body that is forty-seven years old. And I am still not going out there in the dark. Dehydrated does not kill you tonight. A street does. Lie down.

action: press 'Y' -- say yes and go to sleep
commentary: It asks whether I am sure, and offers to save the game before I close my eyes, which is a strange kind of mercy from a house. Yes. And look at the yard while I answer it: footprints. Yellow footprints all over the ground east and south of this building, dozens of them, in the dirt and on the path and out along the road. That is what has been walking round me since eight o'clock this morning and there was never only one.

action: press '9' -- set the alarm for nine hours, to wake at first light
commentary: It asks if I want an alarm and offers me three hours through to nine. Nine. It is six minutes past eight now and nine hours puts me at five past five in the morning, and the sun comes up over this part of the state at about half four at the end of May. That is first light with a whole day in front of it. That is the entire plan. Sleep, wake, find water before the town wakes up.

action: press 'bar' -- lie there and let the time run, because sleep is not coming on command
commentary: This is a comfortable place to sleep, it told me, and then: you lie down preparing to fall asleep. And then nothing. Twenty past eight, flat on my back under a stranger's blanket with the alarm set, and the rest bar is empty because I have not done a thing all day except sit. I am not tired. I am an insomniac who is not tired, at eight in the evening, and I have known since I was thirty how this goes. You do not fall asleep. You lie there and wait to be allowed to.

action: press 'w' -- wait rather than set another alarm
commentary: Wait.

action: press '8' -- let six hours run while I lie here
commentary: Six hours. Twenty past eight to twenty past two in the morning, lying still in the dark with my eyes shut and my ears open, and somewhere in the middle of that it will take me whether I agree to it or not. It always has.

action: press '5' -- lie still and let one turn go by
commentary: Three times I reached for the clock and three times nothing happened -- the screen did not move a pixel and the watch stayed at six minutes past eight. Something in this house is not listening to me. So stop asking it for hours and ask it for one second. Lie still. Count one.

action: press 'I' -- answer the question that was on the screen the whole time
commentary: And there it is, and I am the one who was not listening. It has been sitting in the middle of the screen since I set the alarm: you start having withdrawals, stop trying to fall asleep? Four times I answered a question nobody had asked and ignored the one that was actually in front of me. That is what being twenty-six years into a pack a day and nine hours out of the last cigarette does to a person. No. I am not getting up. Ignore it and let me sleep.

action: press 'I' -- ignore the crash and keep my eyes shut
commentary: A crash now, from the east and above me, the second one tonight. Something on the floor over my head has knocked something over. I am not going up there in the dark with a peeler. Ignore it.

action: press 'I' -- dismiss the engine's own error report and let it stop repeating
commentary: The screen has gone black and white and the game itself is talking to me now rather than the survivor: an error has occurred, a tough zombie cannot climb over a dumpster, source file monmove dot cpp, line seventeen seventy-nine. That is the engine's own complaint about its own pathfinding and it has nothing to do with me. Dismiss it, and tell it not to raise the same one again, because there is a whole night of that thing walking into a dumpster ahead of us.

action: press 'I' -- dismiss the same engine error again and ask it once more to stay quiet
commentary: The same report again, word for word, same file, same line. Whatever is out there has walked into that dumpster twice. Dismiss it again and ask again for it to be ignored.

action: press 'C' -- keep trying to fall asleep and stop being asked about it
commentary: Half past eight and the game has finally asked me the only question that matters tonight. You have trouble sleeping, keep trying? Stop and get up, continue, or continue and do not ask again. Continue, and do not ask again. I have been having trouble sleeping since 2016 and the answer has never once been to get up.

action: press 'space' -- put the notice away and go back to sleep
commentary: Twenty past eight until quarter past two, tossing and turning, and then: you fall asleep. And then a dream, and I am going to write the dream down exactly as it came because I am not going to pretend to be a better person than I am. In it I took several of them apart with my hands and then went through their clothes looking for a cigarette that had not been smoked. That is what is left of me at two in the morning. And over the top of it the house has put up a green notice: achievement completed, the first day of the rest of their unlives, survive for a day and find a safe place to sleep. Year one, May the twenty-first, quarter past two in the morning. I will take it.

action: press 'S' -- save the game and stop for the night
commentary: Awake. Not by the alarm -- the alarm was set for five past five and it is quarter past two. Something is making noise, it says, and then another crash from the south-east and above, and then: you wake up. I stretched and my muscles are not doing so good today, in red, and I am dehydrated, and my speed is seventy-one out of a hundred, and I am on my feet in the dark in a stranger's bedroom on the twenty-first of May. That is the first day. One blade, one needle, one bottle, one book, socks, a shirt, a blanket and a door I shut myself. No water. And I am still here, which yesterday morning I would not have put money on. Save it.

action: press 'Y' -- answer yes and let the house write everything down
commentary: Save and quit, it asks, yes or no. Yes. Everything I did today is going down on that disk exactly as it happened, including the four times I pushed at a wall, the fridge with nothing in it, the toilet I did not find until five in the afternoon, and the dream about the cigarettes. I did not cheat. I did not once ask this game for anything it would not have given a real woman standing in that room. Tomorrow I go out the south door at first light with a bottle in my pocket and I find water. Delphine Ouellette, forty-seven, of Mount Chase, Maine. End of day one.
